subject: Initial token window & stepped throughput exception request
messages:
From: Joni Silver <joni@fastpay.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Keisha Thomas <keisha.thomas@fastpay.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial token window and throughput expectations for FastPay POC

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a short POC and procurement asked me to pin down a couple of SLA items before we sign the pilot SOW: specifically the time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints and sustained token/sec expectations during peak processing.

Background: our use case streams a large initial system prompt (20–30k tokens) and then many short user turns; we care about the first token arriving quickly for perceived latency, but we also have a bursty steady-state during peak reconciliation jobs (~10-15 concurrent streams).

Questions:
- What are Redwood’s standard commitments (p95) for TTFT on streaming vs non-streaming endpoints?
- What sustained tokens/sec can we expect on a Dedicated pool vs Hosted for a single tenant at our scale?
- Is Redwood able to provide a temporary SLA carveout (e.g., relax TTFT for first 30s of large context loads, with a guaranteed stepped throughput curve thereafter) while we iterate on prompt engineering and KV-cache warmup?

If you need logs or an example workload, I can attach samples — I’ve copied Keisha from procurement/legal to make sure we capture any contract riders early.

Best,
Joni
Head of Engineering, FastPay
joni@fastpay.io
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Joni Silver <joni@fastpay.io>
Cc: Keisha Thomas <keisha.thomas@fastpay.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial token window and throughput expectations for FastPay POC

Joni — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front, then a recommended next step.

High-level: Redwood’s baseline public SLAs differ for streaming vs sync (non-streaming) primarily because streaming delivers partial payloads and we optimize for steady emission. Typical expectations (hosted):
- Non-streaming (sync) TTFT (p95): ~250–350 ms for short-context requests.
- Streaming first-token (p95): ~350–600 ms depending on model variant and context size.
- Sustained emission: our engine can sustain thousands of tokens/sec across a Dedicated pool; per-connection sustained rates are gated by model and kernel (typical per-stream steady-state 50–500 tokens/sec depending on instance class).

Regarding your carveout ask: we can offer a timeboxed SLA modification for the POC. Suggested carveout we’ve seen work:
- Initial-token window: relax TTFT obligation for the first 20–40 seconds on requests where context > 10k tokens (explicitly enumerated), provided we hit a stepped throughput guarantee after warmup (e.g., 50 TPS for first 30s, 200 TPS thereafter up to the Dedicated pool capacity).
- Duration: 30-day pilot exception, after which we’ll revisit with logs/measurements.
- Operational controls: we’d need sample traffic, a representative key set, and an SLO exception form to track the scope.

Next step: I’ve looped Rachel (SRE/product) to help quantify the stepped curve and capture what we’ll need on the FastPay side (sample logs, typical batch sizes, and peak concurrency). If you’re comfortable, please share a small trace file (or let us take a short perf capture during a 30-minute run).

I’ll draft a short SOW rider once Rachel confirms the technical numbers.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Sales (Platform) | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Joni Silver <joni@fastpay.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Keisha Thomas <keisha.thomas@fastpay.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial token window and throughput expectations for FastPay POC

Hi all — quick technical note and attachment list. I dug into similar pilots and sketched a conservative stepped-throughput profile below. Attaching a template SLO exception form and a sample latency bundle from a prior customer for reference.

Conservative stepped-throughput proposal (per-stream):
- Cold window (0–30s): no strict TTFT SLA; expect first-token p95 up to ~5–6s when serving massive system prompts (20–30k) unless prefix caching is pre-warmed.
- Warmed steady state (30–300s): target 75 tokens/sec p95 per stream on our medium-grade dedicated nodes (can be higher for high-end reserved GPU classes).
- Scale: we’ll size the Dedicated pool to ensure aggregate capacity for your 10–15 concurrent streams plus overhead; we recommend a 20% headroom buffer during the pilot.

Requirements from FastPay to make the carveout safe and reversible:
- A sample trace (packetized) or a 10-minute run capturing the largest system prompt and a representative user-turn distribution (attach as ZIP).
- Identification of which requests qualify for the carveout (e.g., requests with header X-FP-Large-Context: true or explicit context-length > 10k).
- Agreement that Redwood can throttle or fallback to smaller model variant if downstream queuing exceeds thresholds.

Attachments: slo-exception-form.pdf; system_latency_logs_20260412.zip

If FastPay can send the sample trace, we’ll run a quick profile on our internal staging fleet and return a concrete p95 table and number of Dedicated nodes to request in the SOW.

-rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
